description: A three-input mixer feeding a four-stage shift register, with two feedback paths from the last stage back into the mixer

params.text: Scales OUT 4 into a modelled diode before that feedback reaches the mixer, 0 to 4; the diode squares its input, so the effect grows far faster than the knob turns
Scales whatever arrives at IN 3 into the mixer, passing nothing fully anticlockwise and full level fully clockwise; with IN 3 empty it scales OUT 4 back into the mixer instead

inputs.text: Added into the mixer at full level
Added into the mixer through the IN 3 knob; with nothing patched, that knob feeds OUT 4 back into the mixer instead
Moves the register on one stage at each rise above 1V

outputs.text: The mixer's total clamped to -10V to 10V, taken afresh on every fourth clock and held between times
The value OUT 1 took, copied here one clock later
The value OUT 1 took, copied here two clocks later
The value OUT 1 took, copied here three clocks later, and the one both feedback controls read

notes: nothing moves without a clock: patch one into CLOCK and the four outputs fill in turn, OUT 1 taking a new mixer value on every fourth clock.
both feedback knobs come up fully anticlockwise, so with nothing patched all four outputs stay at 0V however fast the clock runs.
the linear feedback path is the IN 3 knob and it is only there while IN 3 is empty; the nonlinear path through the diode is always in circuit and is subtracted rather than added.

inputs.0:
bipolar · continuous · one channel only

the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±10V.
inputs.1:
bipolar · continuous · one channel only

the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±10V.
inputs.2:
bipolar · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads the OUT 4 voltage; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±10V.
inputs.3: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
